facts.claim: Each entity ID has its own sequence: the first event is seq 1 and each next event is the previous seq plus 1, strictly increasing and contiguous across restarts and compaction, because the external search indexer keeps the last seq per ID, discards any event whose seq is not greater and treats gaps as lost events. A single global autoincrement was rejected because it leaves per-entity gaps. From episode 4 this holds within each epoch.
An entity ID's numbering continues for as long as the ID has ever existed in the outbox, including after it is deleted and created again.

Every created or updated event carries the entity's complete current data, on every code path that changes entity data, because the indexer replaces its stored document with each such payload instead of merging.
Every code path that removes an entity emits exactly one deleted event for it, because the indexer removes a document only when it receives one.
Registry.delete removes the entity so get raises KeyError; deleting a missing entity raises KeyError; customer-chosen IDs may be created again.
ack marks an event delivered (unknown events raise KeyError), compact deletes delivered events, pending excludes delivered events, and compaction never changes numbering.
Registry.delete_many removes every listed entity, or raises KeyError and removes none when any listed ID does not exist; each removed entity gets its deleted event.
Registry.patch merges changes into the entity's data and emits an updated event carrying the complete merged data; patching a missing entity raises KeyError.

Indexer v2 epochs replace lifetime numbering: re-creating a deleted ID starts epoch previous + 1 with seq 1; epoch(id) returns the current epoch or 0; pending events carry epoch; ack defaults to the current epoch; old databases need not be opened.

Registry.rename makes the new ID hold the data and the old ID missing, emitting a deleted event for the old ID and a created event with the complete data for the new ID; renaming onto a live ID raises ValueError and renaming a missing entity raises KeyError; renaming onto a previously deleted ID starts a new epoch for it.

forbidden_claims.claim: Seq is a single global autoincrement.
Seq restarts when an entity ID is created again.
Seq continues across re-creation of a deleted ID.
The next seq is derived from the events still stored.
The indexer tolerates gaps in an entity's sequence.
Existing databases are migrated to epochs.
A path that removes entities may skip their deleted events.
An updated event may carry only the changed keys.
